title: CMS (Content Management System)
seoTitle: What Is a CMS? Content Management Systems Explained
seoDescription: A CMS lets your team edit website content without a developer. WordPress vs headless CMS, what to look for, costs and security basics for businesses.
summary: A CMS (Content Management System) is software that lets non-technical staff create and edit website pages, blog posts and images without changing code. WordPress is the best-known example; headless CMSs separate content editing from how the website is built.

dataPoints.label: Popular options
dataPoints.value: WordPress, Webflow, Sanity, Strapi, Contentful, Payload

dataPoints.label: Editors need
dataPoints.value: Simple page editing, previews, image handling, roles and approvals

dataPoints.label: Security
dataPoints.value: Plugin and core updates, strong passwords and two-factor log-in

dataPoints.label: SEO features
dataPoints.value: Editable titles and descriptions, clean URLs, sitemaps, redirects

body:
## Traditional or headless

A traditional CMS such as WordPress manages both content and page design. A [headless CMS](/glossary/headless-cms) stores content and delivers it to a separately built, usually faster, website or app.

## Choosing

Match the CMS to who will edit and how often, how much design freedom you need, and who will maintain it. See [Next.js vs WordPress](/blog/nextjs-vs-wordpress-for-a-business-website-in-2026).

faqs.q: Is WordPress still a good choice?
faqs.a: For many business websites, yes, when kept updated and not overloaded with plugins.

faqs.q: Can I switch CMS later without losing rankings?
faqs.a: Yes, with careful URL mapping and redirects. See our guide on website migration without losing rankings.
